contributions.title: Bind PDA signer seeds in take_and_close and refund; remove debug println!; fix token list query key
contributions.author: Blockchains

narrative.problem: On the deployed devnet program take_and_close aborted with an access violation, so an escrow could be created but never taken; refund used the same signer-seed pattern.
alternatives: Keep the temporaries and rebuild with a different toolchain (fragile: the failure depends on code generation)
Store the bump and escrow id bytes in the state account and borrow from there
risks: Program changes need a redeploy; existing escrows created by the old program keep their PDAs (seeds are unchanged, so they remain takeable).
Frontend token query changes affect only the dropdown data source.
limitations: The Sol.College runtime fixture also passes on the upstream baseline a9c3a41 with Solana 1.18.26 platform tools: it does not reproduce the toolchain-dependent devnet crash. It proves the candidate's create/take/refund economics and negative cases on a local validator.
Frontend changes are not exercised by the fixture.
This is a Sol.College demonstration: acceptance is by Sol.College's own reviewer, not by the upstream project.
narrative.integration: Merge the three commits onto upstream main (fast-forward from a9c3a41), rebuild with Anchor 0.30.1, redeploy to devnet, then run contract/tests/take-and-close.ts.
narrative.rollback: Redeploy the previous program binary (program upgrade authority) and revert the three commits; account layouts are unchanged.

testConclusions: Exact candidate built with Anchor 0.30.1 / Solana 1.18.26 in the untrusted, secret-free job.

Runtime fixture on solana-test-validator: create, duplicate create rejected, outsider refund rejected, take swaps 10 A for 5 B and closes vault and state, repeat take rejected, take with insufficient balance rejected, refund returns the deposit.
Negative control e288388 (maker underpaid by one base unit) must be rejected by the same fixture.
